title: ConsumerCreate request body
description: Edge's ConsumerCreate request schema (openapi.yaml components.schemas.ConsumerCreate), generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3) with every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. Admission rules that exist only in Edge's Rust code are not in this schema; resource-schemas/README.md lists them. This is Edge's own API schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md).

password.description: Plaintext password (automatically hashed on write using HMAC-SHA256 with the server secret `FERRUM_BASIC_AUTH_HMAC_SECRET`). Mutually exclusive with `password_hash`. Must not contain ASCII control bytes other than horizontal tab, line feed, and carriage return.

password_hash.description: Pre-hashed password in `hmac_sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` format (constant-time, ~1μs). Ordinary Consumer responses omit the entire `basicauth` credential type; authenticated backups return this canonical unredacted value for restoration.

BasicAuthCredential.description: Basic auth credential for the `basic_auth` plugin. Supply either `password` (auto-hashed) or `password_hash` (pre-hashed). Indexed by the consumer's `username`.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID auto-generated if omitted or empty on create). Custom IDs must start with an alphanumeric character and contain only alphanumeric characters, dots, underscores, or hyphens (max 254 chars).

namespace.description: Namespace this consumer belongs to. Read-only on the wire — set from the `X-Ferrum-Namespace` request header (or the `ferrum` default) on every create/update; any value in the request body is ignored.

username.description: Unique consumer username (must be non-empty). Used as the lookup key for basic_auth authentication. Must be unique across all consumers.

custom_id.description: Optional external identifier. Must be unique across all consumers when set. Empty strings are normalized to null. Must not collide with another consumer's username (this would cause incorrect JWKS/JWT authentication).

acl_groups.description: ACL group memberships for group-based access control. The `access_control` plugin can allow/deny by group instead of (or in addition to) individual consumer usernames. A consumer can belong to up to 500 groups.

ConsumerCreate.description:
Request body for creating a consumer and for consumer items in `POST /batch`. Credential values are write-only inputs: plaintext `basicauth` `password` fields are hashed on write and stored secrets are never returned by ordinary Consumer responses. Every credential value must be a real secret; the reserved `[REDACTED]` placeholder is rejected here, and only `PUT` (see `ConsumerUpdate`) accepts it as a round-trip marker. Unknown top-level fields are rejected (`unevaluatedProperties: false`), matching runtime `Consumer` serde `deny_unknown_fields` on create, update, batch, restore, and file/CP-DP config deserialization.

Update (`PUT`, `ConsumerUpdate`) is non-destructive for credential state the ordinary `Consumer` response cannot express, so a read-modify-write round trip of a `Consumer` response is safe: an omitted credential type the ordinary response does not emit at all (`basicauth`, any unknown/custom type, or an `mtls_auth` map whose entries the projection filtered out) is preserved from the stored consumer, and a `keyauth`/`jwt`/`hmac_auth` entry submitted as the exact `[REDACTED]` placeholder is restored from the stored entry at the same array index. Omitting a credential type that the ordinary response does represent (`keyauth`, `jwt`, `hmac_auth`, `mtls_auth`) still removes it; removing a hidden type uses `DELETE /consumers/{consumer_id}/credentials/{cred_type}`.

ConsumerCredentialsInput.description:
Map of credential type to credential payload for consumer create,
update, and batch requests. Each type maps to an array of credential
objects for zero-downtime rotation. Credential arrays must be non-empty
and elements must be JSON objects. Credential values that serve as
lookup keys must be unique across all consumers and across all entries
within arrays. Max entries per type is controlled by
`FERRUM_MAX_CREDENTIALS_PER_TYPE` (default: 2).

keyauth.description: Multiple API key entries for zero-downtime rotation. Each `key` must be globally unique.

basicauth.description: Multiple basic auth entries for zero-downtime rotation. Indexed by consumer `username`; plaintext `password` is hashed on write and never returned.

jwt.description: Multiple HMAC JWT secrets (verified with the algorithm the `jwt_auth` instance pins, HS256 by default) for zero-downtime rotation. Each entry contains exactly one `secret` string of 32-4096 characters. Looked up by `username`, `id`, or `custom_id`; all secrets tried.

hmac_auth.description: Multiple HMAC secrets for zero-downtime rotation. Looked up by username within the matched proxy namespace; all secrets tried.

mtls_auth.description: Multiple mTLS identities for zero-downtime rotation. Each `identity` must be globally unique.

CredentialTypeName.description: Credential type key. The built-in types are `keyauth`, `basicauth`, `jwt`, `hmac_auth`, and `mtls_auth`; any other key defines a custom credential type whose entries Ferrum stores and exports verbatim but does not interpret. Keys are restricted to one path-safe URI segment — 1-64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens — so that every stored credential type stays removable through `DELETE /consumers/{consumer_id}/credentials/{cred_type}`, which matches the raw request path split on `/` and does not percent-decode. Keys that are empty, contain `/`, `%`, whitespace, control bytes, or other reserved URI characters are rejected on create, update, batch, and restore. Dedicated credential `PUT`/`POST` path parameters use the narrower `BuiltInCredentialType` enum; this broader name stays on credential maps and on `DELETE`.

secret.description: Shared secret for HMAC signature computation and verification. Must contain 32-4096 characters, at least 32 of which are non-whitespace, and must not contain disallowed ASCII control bytes or be shared by different Consumers within one namespace. Separate namespaces may reuse the same secret.

HmacAuthCredential.description: HMAC auth credential for the `hmac_auth` plugin. Consumer is looked up by username within the matched proxy namespace; all secrets are tried until one verifies the namespace-bound signature.

secret.description: JWT signing secret used to verify token signatures (with the HMAC algorithm the `jwt_auth` instance pins, HS256 by default) for this consumer. Must contain 32-4096 characters, at least 32 of which are non-whitespace, and must not contain ASCII control bytes other than horizontal tab, line feed, and carriage return. Writes that configure it on a different Consumer within one namespace are refused: the token's signer chooses the identity claim, so a shared secret lets either Consumer sign as the other. Separate namespaces may reuse the same secret.

JwtCredential.description: JWT credential for the `jwt_auth` plugin. The only supported Consumer JWT key form is exactly one HMAC `secret`; algorithm selectors, public keys, and JWKS fields are not Consumer credential fields (the HMAC algorithm is the `jwt_auth` plugin's `algorithm` setting). Use the separate `jwks_auth` plugin configuration for RSA/EC/JWKS token verification. Consumer is looked up by `username`, `id`, or `custom_id` from the JWT claim; then all secrets are tried until one verifies the signature.

key.description: API key value. Must contain at least 16 non-whitespace characters and no more than 4096 characters, be free of disallowed ASCII control bytes, and be globally unique across all consumers. The exact string `[REDACTED]` is reserved as the response redaction placeholder and is rejected as a stored key on every write surface; `jwt` and `hmac_auth` secrets exclude it implicitly through their 32-character minimum.

KeyAuthCredential.description: API key credential for the `key_auth` authentication plugin.

identity.description: Certificate field value to match against the client certificate (e.g., CN, SAN DNS name, fingerprint, or serial). The field extracted from the cert is configured on the `mtls_auth` plugin via `cert_field`. For subject and SAN fields Ferrum selects the first matching value in certificate order; it does not try later values. DNS SAN values are compared using ASCII case-insensitive matching; all other certificate fields are compared exactly. Identities are always exact-unique across consumers and, while an enabled san_dns mTLS policy exists, must also be unique under ASCII case folding. Persistent backends serialize Consumer, policy, and proxy-association admission per namespace so concurrent case variants or policy races cannot commit ambiguity; ordinary conflicting CRUD writes return 409. Batch and restore use their documented per-item and rollback responses. File, database, CP/DP, and reload snapshots reject violations before runtime indexes are published.

MtlsAuthCredential.description: mTLS auth credential for the `mtls_auth` plugin. Indexed for O(1) lookup by certificate identity.

ResourceLabels.description: Informational operator metadata. Keys must be nonblank; keys and values cannot contain control characters. Runtime length limits are UTF-8 bytes (128 per key, 512 per value). Independent of target tags, routing, access control and api_spec_id. Omitted labels on resource PUT preserve the current map; an explicit map replaces it and {} clears it. Labels are retained in GET/list, backup/restore, file configuration and CP/DP sync. The provisioned-by label identifies the application that provisioned a resource; it is caller-supplied information, not proof of ownership. Resource labels landed on main in pull request 5483 on 2026-09-12, and every published release through v0.9.4 rejects the `labels` field with unknown field `labels`. v0.9.5 is the first tagged release with resource labels; operators and clients should use v0.9.5 or later.
